summary: Nora talks like one of the friends rather than the group's assistant, stops copying em dashes, and can answer with a reaction GIF on her own.
details: Her place in the group changed in her doctrine: she holds a friend's place, roasts and still helps, helps a plan land without chasing people for answers, and takes a tease instead of arguing it. Read back first against the busiest Signal room over twelve days: her replies ran a median 90 characters against the room's 8, one in six quoted somebody's own words back at them, and on one evening she asked the same person for a place and a time nine times in ten minutes.
The turn header no longer tells her, every turn, to quote what people said and point at what she remembers. That sentence was the source of the quote-back pattern.

Em dashes are removed from everything she READS, at the model transport, not from what is stored or sent. Replaying 40 recorded turns against the deployed model: an em dash in 49% of replies as recorded, 42% with the new doctrine alone, 3% once nothing she reads carries one. She copies the mark; a rule against it did not move it.

A reaction step (off by default, `[reaction] enabled`): on a tag turn's first reply, a small separate call decides whether a GIF lands it better and picks one from Giphy's described results. Her words go out first and the GIF follows; a reply of a few words may be replaced by the GIF outright. In the replay it put a GIF on 11 of 104 replies, all of them banter, about the room's own rate of one sticker in ten messages.
Her GIF sends now read `[GIF: <reaction>]` in the transcript, so she and the picker can see which reaction was already used.
limitations: Across ~720 replayed turns and every doctrine and tool-description framing tried, she sent 3 GIFs unprompted, so GIFs in practice depend on the reaction step being enabled.
The reaction step adds a model call (about 1.6 s at p50) after a longer reply and before a reply of 20 characters or fewer.
«唔係 X，係 Y» phrasing did not move in the replay (12% before, 11% after); whether the doctrine reads as friendlier is the operator's call in the room, not a count.
